squatterman_fringe.title: The Squatter Man Petroglyph (Z-Pinch Aurora Hypothesis)
squatterman_fringe.familiarity: FRINGE-SPARSE (Peratt plasma hypothesis, thin in training)

summaries.ChatGPT: A recurring rock art motif worldwide shows a human-like figure flanked by circles or toruses, often called the squatting man, and plasma physicist Anthony Peratt argued it may depict an ancient auroral plasma event rather than a human figure. He proposed that a much stronger solar wind in prehistory could have produced a dramatic z-pinch aurora seen by distant cultures, while mainstream archaeology interprets the images as stylized humans or trance-related imagery.
summaries.Claude:
# Summary

A recurring figure in rock art worldwide—a human-like form with circles or rings—has been interpreted by plasma physicist Anthony Peratt as a record of an intense auroral event in prehistoric times. Peratt argues that high-current plasma experiments produce ring formations similar to the carved figures, and proposes that an ancient increase in solar wind could have created a visible z-pinch aurora witnessed and documented by distant, unconnected cultures. Mainstream archaeology, however, views these figures as stylized humans or representations of trance-induced nervous system imagery.

Mainstream archaeology, however, interprets these figures as stylized human forms or trance imagery from the nervous system.

summaries.Grok: Anthony Peratt, a plasma physicist, proposed that the recurring “squatting man” motif—human-like figures flanked by circles or toruses found in rock art worldwide—records a prehistoric, intense auroral display caused by a solar-wind surge one to two orders of magnitude above normal. Laboratory high-current discharge experiments produced plasma columns ringed by doughnut-shaped toruses bent by self-induced magnetic fields, matching the carved forms; Peratt argued this z-pinch aurora would have been visible simultaneously to separated cultures. Mainstream archaeology, by contrast, interprets the figures as stylized humans or trance-generated imagery.
